quizzes.title: Week 1 Language Check: Capitals and sentence types
quizzes.description:
Week 1 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 1
20 points10 questionsOpen-noteOne attempt
Grammar · 1 to 5
Capitals and sentence types
 
Words · 6 to 10
warydeliverancerashcaptivityreproach

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is a proper noun? "Daniel walked to the busy town of Capernaum."
questions.feedback_correct: Capernaum names one particular town, so it takes a capital.
questions.feedback_incorrect: One word shows action, one describes, one names any town. Which names one particular place?

questions.text: Which sentence is capitalized correctly?

answers.text: Thacia and Joel moved from Ketzah to Capernaum.
thacia and joel moved from ketzah to capernaum.
Thacia and Joel moved from ketzah to Capernaum.
Thacia And Joel Moved From Ketzah To Capernaum.

questions.feedback_correct: Every name of a person or place has a capital, and nothing else does.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Capitalize the names of people and places, every one of them, and leave ordinary words small.

questions.text: What type of sentence is this? "Did Joel tell you I've kept at my trade?"
questions.feedback_correct: Daniel is asking Simon something, so it is interrogative and ends with a question mark.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Is Daniel telling, asking, giving an order, or crying out? Look at the end mark.

questions.text: Which sentence is imperative?
questions.feedback_correct: Rosh tells Daniel to do something: that is imperative.
questions.feedback_incorrect: An imperative sentence tells someone to do something. Which one gives an order?

questions.text: Joel kneels in the passage and cries, "I will take the oath too___" Which end mark shows his strong feeling?
questions.feedback_correct: Joel is crying out with strong feeling: an exclamation point.
questions.feedback_incorrect: He is not asking, and this is no calm statement. Which mark shows strong feeling?

questions.text: "Slowly, like a wary animal, Daniel took a few steps back and let himself down on the grass." Wary means
questions.feedback_correct: Daniel moves slowly, ready to run if he must.
questions.feedback_incorrect: How does an animal move when it is not sure it is safe?

questions.text: Thacia says, "We know that deliverance will come." Deliverance is

answers.text: a heavy tax paid to Rome
a message carried from village to village

questions.feedback_correct: She means the Jews will one day be set free from the Romans.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Thacia is talking about the Romans not being there forever. What will come?

questions.text: Hezron says of Daniel's father, "He was a good man, your father, but a rash one." Rash means

answers.text: acting too fast, without thinking about what could happen

questions.feedback_correct: Hezron thinks Jamin acted too quickly.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Hezron says 'good, but…'. What kind of flaw would worry a careful man like Hezron?

questions.text: Hezron says, "In his heart every Jew grieves at our captivity." Captivity is

answers.text: being held prisoner; not being free

questions.feedback_correct: Hezron means his people are not free in their own land.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Daniel has just said his people are prisoners on their own land. Which choice matches?

questions.text: At the meal in Bethsaida Joel eats without washing his hands, and "He too must have felt the carpenter's words as a reproach." A reproach is

answers.text: words that tell someone he has done wrong

questions.feedback_correct: Joel has just broken a rule he has kept all his life, and the words sting.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Joel has just done something his father would call wrong. How would the teacher's words feel to him?

quizzes.title: Week 2 Language Check: Verbs and tense
quizzes.description:
Week 2 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 2
20 points10 questionsOpen-noteOne attempt
Grammar · 1 to 5
Verbs and tense
 
Words · 6 to 10
miserderisiveaccountablerecompensemisgiving

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is the verb? "Daniel carried the old man to the side of the road."
questions.feedback_correct: Carried shows the action.
questions.feedback_incorrect: One choice names a person, one describes, one names a place. Which word shows what Daniel did?

questions.text: What tense is the verb in "Leah weaves fine cloth for a widow in Chorazin"?
questions.feedback_correct: Weaves is happening now, or happens again and again.
questions.feedback_incorrect: There is no -ed ending and no will. When is the weaving happening?

questions.text: Which sentence keeps a steady tense?

answers.text: Daniel banks the fire and bolted the door.
Daniel banked the fire and bolts the door.
Daniel bank the fire and bolting the door.
Daniel banked the fire and bolted the door.

questions.feedback_correct: Banked and bolted are both past.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the sentence where both verbs are past tense.

questions.text: Which change replaces a weak verb with a stronger, more exact one? "Daniel went into the shop and shut the door."

answers.text: "Daniel moved into the shop and shut the door."
"Daniel flung himself into the shop and shut the door."
"Daniel got into the shop and shut the door."
"Daniel came into the shop and shut the door."

questions.feedback_correct: Flung himself shows how fast and how hard he moved.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Three choices swap one vague verb for another. Which one paints the action?

questions.text: Which fixes the tense slip in "Joel gets fish from Simon and Andrew and peddled them in the city"?

answers.text: Joel got fish from Simon and Andrew and peddled them in the city.
Joel got fish from Simon and Andrew and peddles them in the city.
Joel gets fish from Simon and Andrew and will peddled them in the city.
Joel getting fish from Simon and Andrew and peddled them in the city.

questions.feedback_correct: Got and peddled: both past, steady.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Make both verbs past tense, and keep them correct.

questions.text: "Why should one greedy old miser live like a king in Antioch while his fellow Jews toiled and starved?" A miser is

answers.text: a beggar who travels the back roads
a person who hoards money and hates to spend it
a tax collector who works for Rome
a merchant who trades in gold

questions.feedback_correct: He has a bag of gold and still lives like a pauper.
questions.feedback_incorrect: He only pretends to be a beggar. What does he do with his money?

questions.text: "Rosh shot a derisive glance from under the black brows." Derisive means

answers.text: mocking, showing that you think someone is foolish

questions.feedback_correct: Rosh says, 'So he took you in with his whining!' He is mocking Daniel.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read what Rosh says right after the glance.

questions.text: Simon says, "An outlaw may think he is accountable to no one." Accountable means

answers.text: friendly and easy to talk to
responsible; expected to answer for what you do

questions.feedback_correct: In a village, Simon says, every man answers for his neighbors' safety.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read Simon's next sentence: who holds his neighbor's safety in his hands?

questions.text: "He realized that she had never before known any recompense for her hours at the loom." Recompense is

answers.text: payment or reward for work or trouble

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel has just put a silver coin in her hand for her cloth.
questions.feedback_incorrect: What has Daniel just laid in Leah's hand?

questions.text: "Daniel felt not envy, but unexpected misgiving." A misgiving is

answers.text: a feeling of doubt or worry that something may go wrong

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel's next thought is 'If anything went wrong?'
questions.feedback_incorrect: Envy is the feeling he does not have. What does he wonder next?

quizzes.title: Week 3 Language Check: Adjectives and appositives
quizzes.description:
Week 3 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 3
20 points10 questionsOpen-noteOne attempt
Grammar · 1 to 5
Adjectives and appositives
 
Words · 6 to 10
reprisalindignantincredulousdignityheedless

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is an adjective? "Leah, sitting in the lamplight, raised her golden head."
questions.feedback_correct: Golden describes Leah's head: what kind of head.
questions.feedback_incorrect: One choice names a thing, and two show actions. Which word tells what her head is like?

questions.text: In "The parched brown fields drank in the moisture," which word does the adjective parched describe?
questions.feedback_correct: The fields are parched: dry and thirsty.
questions.feedback_incorrect: An adjective sits close to the noun it describes. Which thing is dry?

questions.text: "Andrew, one of the disciples, told the waiting crowd that the master was very weary." What is the appositive?
questions.feedback_correct: One of the disciples renames Andrew, set off by commas.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the words between the commas that tell who Andrew is.

questions.text: Which sentence punctuates the appositive correctly?

answers.text: Simon Daniel's old friend, walked beside him in the dark.
Simon, Daniel's old friend walked beside him in the dark.
Simon Daniel's old friend walked beside him in the dark.
Simon, Daniel's old friend, walked beside him in the dark.

questions.feedback_correct: One comma before the appositive and one after it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: An appositive in the middle of a sentence needs a comma on each side.

questions.text: Which sentence uses an appositive to rename a character?

answers.text: Leah touched the flowers in her golden hair.
The crowd shouted on the dark hillside.
Joktan, Daniel's cheerful helper, fetched water every morning.
Daniel walked the miles back to the village alone.

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel's cheerful helper renames Joktan.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look for a noun phrase that renames a person, set off by commas.

questions.text: "Nor did Roman offers of reward or threats of reprisal produce a single hint of its whereabouts." (Ch. 17) A reprisal is

answers.text: a punishment given back in return for something done against you
a hiding place for stolen goods

questions.feedback_correct: The Romans threaten to punish the village for the lost catapult.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The reward is the other offer in the sentence. What is the threat?

questions.text: "Some men praised Rosh's daring … But more, like this man, were indignant." (Ch. 17) Indignant means

answers.text: pleased with how things turned out
angry because something seems unfair or wrong

questions.feedback_correct: Most villagers are angry that Rosh's men rob and ruin.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Some men praised Rosh. 'But more' felt the opposite. What did they feel?

questions.text: "'Nothing?' Nathan cried out, incredulous." (Ch. 18) Incredulous means

answers.text: not able to believe what you are hearing

questions.feedback_correct: Nathan cannot believe Rosh will do nothing for Joel.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Nathan asks 'Nothing?' as a question. What does that show?

questions.text: "She raised her head and looked at him with such a strange dignity that he backed away." (Ch. 22) Dignity is

answers.text: a calm, serious way of carrying yourself that earns respect

questions.feedback_correct: Leah's calm, steady look makes Daniel step back.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Daniel backs away. What in Leah's look would make a shouting brother step back?

questions.text: "Then, heedless of the master's weariness, … he poured out the story of Rosh." (Ch. 21) Heedless means
questions.feedback_correct: Daniel is so full of guilt that he pays no attention to how tired Jesus is.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read on in the book: he forgets 'everything but the guilt.' How much is he noticing?

quizzes.title: Week 4 Language Check: Participial phrases
quizzes.description:
Week 4 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 4
20 points10 questionsOpen-noteOne attempt
Grammar · 1 to 5
Participial phrases and periodic sentences
 
Words · 6 to 10
indifferentdupeddreadrejectedliberating

questions.text: In "Joktan sat outside the shop, halfheartedly filing down a set of nails," which words are the participial phrase?

answers.text: halfheartedly filing down a set of nails

questions.feedback_correct: Built on filing, it describes Joktan.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the -ing word and the words that go with it. Which group describes Joktan?

questions.text: In "Dazed, Daniel struggled to his feet," which word is the participle?
questions.feedback_correct: Dazed is a verb form that describes Daniel.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Struggled is what Daniel does. Which word describes him before he does it?

questions.text: Which sentence places the comma correctly?

answers.text: Standing, in the blazing sunshine Marcus kept his eyes on the house.
Standing in the blazing sunshine Marcus, kept his eyes on the house.
Standing in the blazing sunshine Marcus kept his eyes, on the house.
Standing in the blazing sunshine, Marcus kept his eyes on the house.

questions.feedback_correct: The comma comes after the whole opening phrase, right before Marcus.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Where do the describing words end and the person begin? The comma goes there.

questions.text: Which sentence has a dangling phrase (it describes the wrong noun)?

answers.text: Waking from the fever, Leah looked up into the master's face.
Laying aside the bottle of leeches, the house grew quiet.
Laying aside the bottle of leeches, the physician shook his head.
Scratching a message on broken pottery, Daniel sent word to Thacia.

questions.feedback_correct: A house cannot lay anything aside. The physician did.
questions.feedback_incorrect: In each sentence, ask who did the opening action. Is that who comes right after the comma?

questions.text: Which is a periodic sentence (the main idea held to the end)?

answers.text: Jesus stood in the doorway in his white robe.
Jesus stood in the doorway, framed against the sunlight.
Framed in the doorway, against the sunlight, stood Jesus in his white robe.
Jesus stood in the doorway, and the sunlight was behind him.

questions.feedback_correct: The details come first; stood Jesus waits until the end.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the main idea, who does what. In which sentence do you wait for it?

questions.text: Daniel works "to keep alive a girl who was indifferent that she lived." Indifferent means

answers.text: not caring one way or the other

questions.feedback_correct: Leah has stopped caring whether she lives.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Daniel cares if she lives. What has Leah stopped doing?

questions.text: "How could he be sure that he would not be duped again?" Duped means

answers.text: tricked into trusting the wrong person

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel trusted Rosh and was fooled.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sentence before asks how he could know whom to trust.

questions.text: Daniel came back from the well "heavy with dread that Leah's anguished breathing might have stopped while he was gone." Dread is

answers.text: deep fear of something that may happen
anger at someone who has wronged you
a heavy load carried on the back

questions.feedback_correct: He fears what he may find when he gets home.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read what he is afraid might have happened while he was gone.

questions.text: "He knew that Daniel had rejected him." Rejected means
questions.feedback_correct: Daniel had turned away from what Jesus offered him.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Think back to Ch. 23, when Daniel would not believe Simon's words about him. What had Daniel done?

questions.text: Daniel's tears were "hot and liberating against his hands." Liberating means
questions.feedback_correct: The tears free him from what he has held so long.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look at what Daniel feels just before: the weight is gone. What do the tears do for him?

quizzes.title: Week 5 Language Check: Parallel structure and punctuation
quizzes.description:
Week 5 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 5
20 points10 questionsOpen-noteOne attempt
Grammar · 1 to 5
Parallel structure, colons and semicolons
 
Words · 6 to 10
purposedespairedremorsedefiedburden

questions.text: Which sentence has parallel structure? (Ch. 11–12)

answers.text: In the village, Daniel worked the forge, caring for Leah, and he gathered a band of boys.
In the village, Daniel working the forge, cared for Leah, and a band of boys.
In the village, Daniel works the forge, cares for Leah, and gathers a band of boys.
In the village, Daniel works the forge, to care for Leah, and gathering a band of boys.

questions.feedback_correct: Works, cares, gathers: every item has the same shape.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read the three actions aloud. Find the choice where all three match.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a colon correctly? (Ch. 5)

answers.text: Hezron says the Zealots have three things to show for their fighting: rows of crosses, burning villages, and heavier taxes.
Hezron says the Zealots have: rows of crosses, burning villages, and heavier taxes.
Hezron says: the Zealots have three things to show for their fighting, rows of crosses, burning villages, and heavier taxes.
Hezron says the Zealots have three things to show for their fighting, rows of crosses: burning villages and heavier taxes.

questions.feedback_correct: A full sentence comes first, then the colon introduces the list.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A colon needs a complete sentence before it. Which choice gives one, then the list?

questions.text: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly? (Ch. 18)

answers.text: Rosh refuses to help Joel; and Daniel goes himself.
Rosh refuses; to help Joel, so Daniel goes himself.
Rosh refuses to help Joel; because Joel was caught.
Rosh refuses to help Joel; Daniel goes after Joel with nineteen boys.

questions.feedback_correct: Both halves are full sentences, and nothing joins them but the semicolon.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look for a full sentence on both sides and no and, so or because after the semicolon.

questions.text: Which sentence places the participial phrase next to the right person? (Ch. 7)

answers.text: Trembling all over, the story finally ends.
Trembling all over, Daniel finishes his story.
Trembling all over, Joel hears the end of Daniel's story.
Daniel trembling all over, finishes his story.

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel is the one trembling, and his name comes right after the phrase.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Who was trembling when the story ended? That person's name must follow the comma.

questions.text: Which is a periodic sentence, holding its main idea until the end? (Ch. 24)

answers.text: Daniel crosses the road to Marcus after Leah's fever leaves her and Jesus is far down the street.
Daniel crosses the road to Marcus, and Leah's fever is gone, and Jesus is far down the street.
With Leah's fever gone and Jesus already far down the street, Daniel crosses the road to Marcus.
Daniel crosses the road. To Marcus. With Leah's fever gone.

questions.feedback_correct: The reader waits through the details for the main idea: Daniel crosses the road.
questions.feedback_incorrect: In a periodic sentence the main clause comes last. Which choice makes you wait for it?

questions.text: "While she had lost everything, purpose remained to him." (Ch. 24) Purpose means

answers.text: a goal that gives your life or actions a point

questions.feedback_correct: Leah has lost everything; Daniel still has a goal to live for.
questions.feedback_incorrect: What does Daniel still have that Leah has lost?

questions.text: "For the first time he despaired that the day would ever come." (Ch. 20) Despaired means
questions.feedback_correct: Joel is leaving, and Daniel thinks it is the end of everything they worked for.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read the sentence just before it: 'It is the end of everything,' Daniel thought.

questions.text: "In a torment of remorse, Daniel did all the work about the house." (Ch. 23) Remorse is

answers.text: deep sorrow and guilt for a wrong you have done
fear of what will happen next

questions.feedback_correct: He blames himself for what his anger did to Leah, and tries to make up for it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: What has Daniel done to Leah just before this? How would he feel about it?

questions.text: "'I made a vow before God!' he defied Jesus." (Ch. 21) To defy is

answers.text: to stand against someone openly and refuse to give in

questions.feedback_correct: Asked to give up his hate, Daniel holds on to his vow.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Jesus has just asked Daniel to give up his hate. Does Daniel give way?

questions.text: "He had thought of Samson as a burden, as a symbol of his own weakness." (Ch. 21) A burden is

answers.text: a heavy load you have to carry

questions.feedback_correct: Daniel once felt Samson was something heavy he was stuck with.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read the next sentence: Daniel had never thought of Samson as a friend. So what had he thought?

discussions.title: All-Class Forum 1: Two Kinds of Freedom
discussions.html:
All-Class Forum 1: Two Kinds of Freedom
6th Grade ELA · The Bronze Bow · Week 3
25 points1 post + 2 repliesCloses end of Week 3
By Chapter 23, which kind of freedom does the book itself take more seriously?
One kind
By force
Taken back from Rome.
 
The other kind
The teacher's
Simon: “the only chains that matter are fear and hate.” Ch. 23
Judge what Speare chose to show, not which freedom you prefer.
1
Post
your answer
→
2
Read
posts unlock after yours
→
3
Reply
two classmates
Your post
 
›Sentence one takes a position.
›Name one moment from Chapters 1 to 23.
›Answer the strongest objection:
Say the teacher's? Speare makes Daniel's anger easy to feel (Ch. 7, Ch. 19).

Say force? The village turns on Rosh (Ch. 17), and he will not help Joel (Ch. 18).
Your replies
 
Add
Evidence they missed.
Challenge
A weak spot, and why.
Ask
What their post left open.
“I agree” is not a reply. Disagree with the idea, not the person.
Done when
 
☐My first sentence takes a position.
☐I named a moment from Chapters 1 to 23.
☐I answered the strongest objection.
☐I replied twice: add, challenge, or ask.
